newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Truckloads of police prevent Tirana protests.
newsitem.headline: Truckloads of police prevent Tirana protests.

text.p: Hundreds of riot police swarmed through the centre of Tirana on Wednesday to prevent Albania's opposition from staging new anti-government protests, confining several top politicians to their headquarters.

Two truckloads of police descended on the headquarters of the Forum for Democracy opposition alliance and prevented prominent politicians, including Socialist party chief Rexhep Mejdani, from leaving the building.

Bystanders on streetcorners, mainly elderly women, shouted at policemen: "We will turn this into a Vlore" -- a reference to the southern port where three people have died this week in clashes between anti-government protesters and police.

"This is intolerable. All the leaders of the opposition were prevented from taking part on the orders of the interior ministry," Skender Gjinushi, leader of the Social Democratic Party, told Reuters Television.
"They are afraid of demonstrations in Tirana because demonstrations show the government does not have the support of the people."

He said violence was inevitable if the government did not relent and allow peaceful protests by investors who blame authorities for the collapse of pyramid investment schemes. The calamity has left hundreds of thousands of Albanians penniless.
Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi has vowed to crack down on a wave of protests, which he says are organised by leftist extremists.

Vans loaded with khaki-clad riot police circulated slowly throughout the capital's centre. Anyone pausing near central Skanderbeg Square, where protesters failed to stage a rally last weekend, was ushered away.

The Forum, which groups 10 political parties, had scheduled a mid-day protest at Tirana's main stadium, but the Interior Ministry banned the gathering. It calls for creation of a "technocrat government" to deal with the pyramid crisis.
About 5,000 people massed peacefully in the centre of Vlore. The protests in the port have been peaceful since Monday. Other protests had taken place in four towns near the Greek border.
